Synthetic benchmark data

Published

November 21, 2026

The PIE maps carry little signal: about 4 % of cells change, much of it scattered, and every pairing of the benchmark lands within a factor of 2.5 of random allocation. With PIE_DATASET=synthetic, the whole benchmark runs instead on a synthetic landscape with a known change process, so the comparison of estimators and allocators is not drowned out by the lack of anything to learn.

The data have the format of 000-pie-data.r, so every step runs unchanged:

  • lu_{1985,1991,1999}.tif: 1 = forest, 2 = built, 3 = other (the years only label three periods: an initial map and two steps of the process);
  • ef_001.tif accessibility, ef_002.tif site quality, ef_003.tif distance to built land in 1985;
  • 100 m cells in EPSG:26986, n_row × n_col cells; a ragged corner lies outside the study area (NA), as in PIE. Besides making the domain a set of cells rather than a rectangle, this keeps CLUinPy working: its demand step (cluinpy/demand.py, freq_list = arr2.tolist()[:-1]) assumes that the map has no-data cells and drops the last class count, so on a map without any it never allocates the last class.

The process is the one of Fig. 2 (2026-09-paper-figures/000-synthetic-process.r), with its four logistic transitions on accessibility, site quality and the share of each class in the 5 × 5 neighbourhood, but on PIE’s three classes and without the fixed lake, which CLUMondo cannot hold:

transition logit of its probability
other → built −5.5 + 7 · share built + 3 · accessibility
forest → built −7 + 6 · share built + 3 · accessibility
forest → other −5 + 4 · (1 − site quality) + 3 · share other
other → forest −6 + 4 · site quality · (1 − accessibility) + 3 · share forest

Every estimator sees the two drivers and the distance to built land; evoland’s learners also get their neighbourhood counts, Dinamica’s Weights of Evidence its distance-to-class maps.

library(data.table)
library(terra)

source("2026-09-model-comparison/common.r")
only_for_dataset("synthetic")
source("2026-09-paper-figures/000-synthetic-process.r")
out_dir <- data_dir
dir.create(out_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

n_row <- 300L
n_col <- 340L
set.seed(2026L)
template <- terra::rast(
  nrows = n_row,
  ncols = n_col,
  xmin = 200000,
  xmax = 200000 + 100 * n_col,
  ymin = 900000,
  ymax = 900000 + 100 * n_row,
  crs = "EPSG:26986"
)
drivers <- make_drivers(template)

# the initial map of Fig. 2 has classes forest 1, arable 2, urban 3, lake 4; here the lake
# becomes arable ("other") and the codes follow PIE: forest 1, built 2, other 3
initial <- make_landscape(template, drivers)
to_pie <- function(map) terra::classify(map, rbind(c(1, 1), c(2, 3), c(3, 2), c(4, 3)))
from_pie <- function(map) terra::classify(map, rbind(c(1, 1), c(2, 3), c(3, 2)))

# two steps of the process on the PIE codes, through the Fig. 2 codes it is written in
lu_1985 <- to_pie(initial)
lu_1991 <- to_pie(step_process(from_pie(lu_1985), drivers))
lu_1999 <- to_pie(step_process(from_pie(lu_1991), drivers))
lu <- c(lu_1985, lu_1991, lu_1999)
years <- c(1985, 1991, 1999)
names(lu) <- paste0("lu_", years)

dist_built <- terra::distance(terra::ifel(lu_1985 == 2, 1, NA))
ef <- c(drivers$accessibility, drivers$site_quality, dist_built)
names(ef) <- paste0("ef_00", 1:3)

# the study area: everything but a ragged north-east corner (the process ran on the full grid)
xy <- terra::crds(template, df = TRUE)
corner <- (xy$x - terra::xmin(template)) / (100 * n_col) + (xy$y - terra::ymin(template)) / (100 * n_row)
ragged <- terra::values(smooth_field(template, w = 9), mat = FALSE)
outside <- terra::setValues(template, corner + 0.25 * ragged > 1.85)
lu <- terra::mask(lu, outside, maskvalues = TRUE)
ef <- terra::mask(ef, outside, maskvalues = TRUE)
for (i in seq_along(years)) {
  terra::writeRaster(
    lu[[i]],
    file.path(out_dir, paste0("lu_", years[i], ".tif")),
    datatype = "INT1U",
    NAflag = 255,
    overwrite = TRUE
  )
}
for (n in names(ef)) {
  terra::writeRaster(
    ef[[n]],
    file.path(out_dir, paste0(n, ".tif")),
    datatype = "FLT4S",
    NAflag = -9999,
    overwrite = TRUE
  )
}

1 Demand handed to every tool

As in 000-pie-data.r: the observed 1991 → 1999 transition counts and the class totals.

dir.create(outputs_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
lu_values <- as.data.table(terra::values(lu))
setnames(lu_values, as.character(years))
lu_values <- lu_values[!is.na(`1985`)]
fwrite(
  lu_values[
    `1991` != `1999`,
    .(count = .N),
    by = .(id_lulc_anterior = `1991`, id_lulc_posterior = `1999`)
  ][order(id_lulc_anterior, id_lulc_posterior)],
  file.path(outputs_dir, "demand_transitions_1991_1999.csv")
)
fwrite(
  rbindlist(lapply(as.character(years), function(y) {
    lu_values[, .N, by = .(id_lulc = get(y))][, year := as.integer(y)]
  }))[order(year, id_lulc), .(year, id_lulc, N)],
  file.path(outputs_dir, "demand_class_totals.csv")
)

2 Observed change

crosstab_period <- function(a, b) {
  table(
    anterior = terra::values(lu[[a]], mat = FALSE),
    posterior = terra::values(lu[[b]], mat = FALSE)
  )
}

Calibration period, 1985 → 1991:

crosstab_period(1, 2)
        posterior
anterior     1     2     3
       1 43444   353  4244
       2     0 12240     0
       3   721  2285 34894

Validation period, 1991 → 1999:

crosstab_period(2, 3)
        posterior
anterior     1     2     3
       1 39840   354  3971
       2     0 14878     0
       3   744  2225 36169

Share of cells that change, per period:

c(
  calibration = mean(values(lu[[1]]) != values(lu[[2]]), na.rm = TRUE),
  validation = mean(values(lu[[2]]) != values(lu[[3]]), na.rm = TRUE),
  cells_in_study_area = sum(!is.na(values(lu[[1]])))
)
        calibration          validation cells_in_study_area 
       7.743861e-02        7.429136e-02        9.818100e+04 
plot(lu, nc = 3, col = lulc_colours)
plot(ef, nc = 3)
